typical_symptoms: Characteristic rolling and folding of leaves into funnel-like or cylindrical shapes held by fine silken threads
Chewed leaf lamina resulting in ragged, skeletonized, or perforated leaves
Presence of green or translucent caterpillars feeding protected inside the rolled leaves
Accumulation of dark fecal pellets (frass) within leaf rolls
visual_characteristics: Small greenish-grey or pale semi-translucent caterpillar with a shiny dark brown to black head capsule
Leaves visibly rolled inward from edges and tied tightly with silk strands
Chewing damage along leaf margins and veins
Visible silk web strands stretching across leaf folds
lesion_characteristics: Irregular chewed holes and ragged margins rather than distinct pathogen lesions
Desiccated brown leaf edges around chewed zones
Rolled leaf margins bound by silken threads
color_characteristics: Larva is pale translucent green to yellowish-grey
Larval head capsule is dark reddish-brown to black
Chewed leaf tissue turns pale green, yellowing, and eventually dry brown
Frass pellets appear dark brown to black
texture_characteristics: Fine silky web texture on leaf surface
Wrinkled and distorted leaf blade from tightly rolled silk tension
Dry and brittle chewed leaf edges
spatial_patterns: Scattered affected leaves across middle to upper canopy
Irregular patches of missing leaf tissue
distinguishing_features: Distinctive tubular or funnel-like rolling of cotton leaves stitched with visible silk threads
Presence of smooth, greenish-translucent caterpillar with a prominent dark head capsule inside or on the leaf surface
Lack of leaf spot lesions or rust pustules, damage defined entirely by pest feeding and webbed foliage
